author: Mark Atwood
text:
Same workspace-wide boilerplate as bd:JMAP-510h.15. The two beads attack the same code from different angles:

- .15 = the catch-all error message 'unhandled backend error variant' is unactionable.
- .18 = the 5-site match-block boilerplate itself should be extracted to one helper.

Both fixes point at the same helper extraction. Verified the same boilerplate exists in canonical jmap-mail-server (email.rs: 7 copies of BackendSetError::SetError match, submission.rs: 4 copies) — workspace-wide sweep needed, canonical-first per workspace AGENTS.md.

The right unit of work is: extract one helper in jmap-server foundation crate (or in each extension-server's helpers.rs — design decision) that maps BackendSetError -> Value with a stable Display-based discriminator for the catch-all (per .15). Then sweep the call sites across all 8 extension-server crates. .15 + .18 close together.

Recommendation: fold into JMAP-xbeb (already covers similar workspace-wide doc/API gaps) OR file a separate workspace propagation epic specifically for backend-error handling consolidation. Either way, this exceeds single-bead scope.

Filing deferred (not human) per workspace AGENTS.md 'When NOT to file human' rule 2 — this is parked-backlog. The human-decision step (whether to undertake the workspace sweep) is the same one that JMAP-xbeb already represents; this bead does not need a separate human-judgment call.

Cross-ref: bd:JMAP-510h.15 (also human-labeled / awaiting epic decomposition).
